summary: POC scoping focused on benchmark planning and harness integration. Discussed customer workload shapes, streaming vs non-streaming tests, load profiles, success criteria (latency percentiles, cost per 1M tokens, accuracy/regression), and timelines. Agreed next steps to exchange scripts and run a harness session. Some minor transcription errors and filler in the recording.
topics: Success criteria (p50/p95 latency, cost targets, quality/regression)
Benchmark harness integration (customer scripts, infra, auth)
Streaming vs non-streaming behavior and telemetry
Load testing plan and sample run schedule
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we'll kick off — this is Alex from Redwood, and Priya's on the call to cover the technical details.
[00:10] Samira (Beacon): Hi Alex, thanks. We want to scope the POC for benchmark integration; our main ask is to validate cost and latency at our peak workloads and also check streaming for live summarization.
[00:23] Priya (Redwood): Great. Can you remind us of your current baseline — like qps, typical sequence lengths, and what success looks like?
[00:30] Tom (Beacon): Sure, so we're seeing around 80 rps average across our inference cluster, spikes to 350 rps during business hours. Average token length for requests is 220 tokens, but some flows go up to 1,200 for long transcript re-runs.
[00:47] Samira: And the critical metrics are p95 latency under 600ms for short flows, p95 under 2s for long flows, and cost target roughly under $XX per 1M tokens — we can share a ballpark. Also, quality regressions are non-negotiable, so we'll need side-by-side outputs for fidelity checks.
[01:05] Alex: Good, that's helpful. For the harness, we typically need your actual inference scripts or a wrapper that replays requests with realistic timestamps and payloads. Do you have a load generator today?
[01:15] Tom: We have a JMeter-based setup and a set of python scripts that call our current managed endpoint. They do both batched and single-request calls; not fully instrumented for streaming though.
[01:26] Priya: Ok, that's fine. The plan we recommend: 1) Exchange scripts, 2) Redwood provides harness template and config (we'll also provide a lightweight runner), 3) run non-streaming baseline tests, 4) run streaming tests with a smaller sample to check tail latency and correctness, 5) iterate on batching/quantization settings.
[01:44] Samira: Sounds good; timelinewise we want an execution window in the next three weeks.
[01:48] Alex: We can do that. We'll send the harness repo and a checklist; Priya will run the streaming test plan with you.
[01:55] Lena (Beacon Security): Quick security note — we'll need either VPC peering or a temp VPN, KMS integration for keys, and audit logs exported to our SIEM during the POC. Also SOC2 evidence is a pre-req for production but for POC a self-hosted private deployment might be interesting.
[02:12] Priya: We can support a private POC in a customer VPC; for the benchmark runs the easiest initial step is to run against Redwood's hosted temporary tenant with sanitized data. For anything with PHI we recommend customer-hosted or private.
[02:28] Tom: Ok, we'll sanitize the sample dataset for the first pass. Regarding streaming vs non-streaming: our use case is live call summarization, streaming for low-latency partials and final summary. We need to understand how token-level throughput maps to p95 latencies when streaming is enabled.
[02:44] Priya: Right — streaming changes the profile: per-token latency matters and network chunking can add jitter. Our harness can simulate both continuous token streaming and chunked partials. We'll capture per-token latency histograms and application-level latencies.
[03:00] Alex: For success criteria let's write them down: p95 end-to-end for short flows < 600ms, p95 for long flows < 2s, streaming per-token p95 < 150ms, and no more than X% quality regressions on a defined eval set. Does that align?
[03:15] Samira: Yes, though we might tighten streaming p95 to 100ms for some critical paths. We'll confirm offline.
[03:22] Priya: Noted. On the harness integration details: we need your scripts, a lightweight auth token, and dataset samples. We will give you a dockerized harness runner; if you prefer to run in your VPC we can provide an AMI or helm chart.
[03:36] Tom: We'll probably start with the docker runner in our dev environment then, and if that looks good we can spin up the private deployment.
[03:42] Alex: Regarding metrics, we'll emit: p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, vCPU/GPU utilization, and cost estimate. Also we'll attach tracing ids to each request for traceability.
[03:55] Samira: For quality checks, we want a side-by-side diff and a small set of regression prompts — maybe 500 cases — to run with eval script and get BLEU/ROUGE-like metrics plus human spot-checks.
[04:08] Priya: We usually run a micro-eval harness and produce a QA report. We'll include instructions for human sampling.
[04:14] Tom: A few logistics items: do you support streaming over HTTP/2 or do you prefer websockets? Our client stack uses HTTP/2 gRPC in some services.
[04:24] Priya: We support both; for lower overhead with chunked payloads HTTP/2 streaming is fine. We'll note best practices for chunk sizes and connection reuse.
[04:35] Alex: Are there any other vendor evaluations you're running in parallel?
[04:38] Samira: We're looking at Anthropic and a managed endpoint from OpenAI just for comparison on latency/cost. We also have internal on-prem experiments with trimmed models.
[04:46] Alex: Ok we'll make sure our benchmark includes those comparative baselines if you can provide endpoint creds or sample outputs.
[04:53] Samira: Yep. Next steps?
[04:56] Alex: I'll send the harness repo + runbook by Friday (2026-08-14), Samira/Tom you'll share 3 representative scripts and the sanitized dataset by Tue (2026-08-18). Priya will schedule the 90-minute harness run session wk of 2026-08-24.
[05:10] Samira: Agreed. Anything else?
[05:13] Lena: Please include the security checklist and KMS integration docs.
[05:17] Priya: Will do, I'll attach the private deployment checklist and KMS notes.
[05:21] Alex: Great — we'll follow up via the shared doc and I'll update the crm deal with the agreed timelines. Thanks everyone.
[05:27] Samira: Thanks all.
[05:30] [end recording]
